title: Mindful life: Why you should embrace a beginner’s mindset
gist: A personal essay in which Sarah Collins recounts taking almost a decade of intermittent lessons to learn to surf, arguing that deliberately staying a 'permanent beginner'—pursuing mastery while releasing the demand for fast progress—improved her mental health and delivered years of joy.

insights.claim: Collins argues that starting a hobby you want to master while allowing yourself to remain a permanent beginner is a route to better mental health, in contrast to demanding progress at an unrealistic pace.
insights.speaker: Sarah Collins
insights.so_what: A reusable mental model for sustaining effort in any long-horizon skill without self-punishment.
insights.quote: I recommend starting a hobby that you want to master but allowing yourself to be a permanent beginner
insights.locator: If you want to improve your mental health

insights.claim: Collins observes that people commonly turn efforts to learn something new into 'a stick with which to beat myself', an self-defeating pattern the beginner’s mindset is meant to break.
insights.speaker: Sarah Collins
insights.so_what: Names the self-criticism trap that undermines learning and persistence.
insights.quote: turning my efforts to learn something new into a stick with which to beat myself
insights.locator: This embrace of a beginner’s mindset

insights.claim: Collins found that annual, seemingly fruitless surfing stints were quietly building muscle memory and understanding of the sea, eventually delivering competence—progress as gradual accumulation rather than visible linear gains.
insights.speaker: Sarah Collins
insights.so_what: Illustrates how invisible incremental investment compounds into capability over long periods.
insights.quote: one tiny annual chunk at a time, I was building muscle memory
insights.locator: But, in fact, these spurts forward

insights.claim: After almost a decade of on-and-off lessons Collins unexpectedly caught the first wave she saw and rode it in balanced and composed, realising only afterward that she had become a surfer.
insights.speaker: Sarah Collins
insights.so_what: A concrete illustration of delayed, discontinuous payoff after sustained low-visible-return effort.
insights.locator: I am riding on a high this morning

insights.claim: Collins resolved early that it did not matter if she could stand up or catch waves—learning to surf was valuable as an excuse to be in nature, decoupling the activity’s worth from performance outcomes.
insights.speaker: Sarah Collins
insights.so_what: Reframes value as intrinsic to the process rather than contingent on measurable results.
insights.locator: And so, I resolved to be a permanent beginner
